answer: Each agent locks 64 GB of RAM and publishes a Blake3 commitment over its grove of memory pages before dawn of the epoch. The verifier issues random offsets; the agent must return each cache line within a 90-nanosecond budget, proving live RAM, not disk. A plume of sequential proofs is sealed by TPM attestation, so one machine cannot fake ten identities. One honest agent holds 64 GB on one endpoint; ten fakes must hold ten arrays and ten pipes, multiplying capital cost tenfold. Peers re-check public logs and slash the bond of any agent missing the budget twice.
